findings.summary: Concurrent manual flush calls can resolve while newer queued events remain unsent when auto flushing is disabled.
findings.consequence: A caller that enqueues an event during an in-flight flush and then awaits a second explicit flush can observe that second flush resolving before the event has been delivered. In non-auto-flush usage, that leaves telemetry queued until another explicit flush occurs.
findings.evidence: Line 368 returns the already-running #flushing promise. #deliver takes one batch before awaiting delivery, while #enqueueIntake appends later events to #queue; the finally block only calls #scheduleFlush, and #scheduleFlush returns immediately when autoFlush is false. The listed tests cover the same in-flight enqueue case only with autoFlush true at test/unit/observability-browser.spec.ts:1693-1706, so the manual-flush contract is not protected.
findings.recommendation: After awaiting an existing normal flush, loop or start another #deliver pass while #queue still contains events and no exit flush is active, or document/test that flush only waits for the currently active batch. Add a focused autoFlush:false test for enqueue-during-in-flight plus a second flush call.
